comments.title: Comment Submitted by Intellex Capital LLC
comments.ai_summary: Intellex Capital LLC is a firm that uses EB-5 money. They ask USCIS to keep allowing bridge loans that are later repaid with EB-5 capital. They say starting construction with a loan before EB-5 money arrives is normal business practice.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor filed a large PDF. They ask USCIS to not apply new rules to people who already invested and to give full life-cycle protection from filing through green card.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Celona Asset Management (USA) Limited
comments.ai_summary: Celona Asset Management is an investment manager. They wrote about moving investor money to another project if needed and ask for clear rules that protect investors and keep the project workable.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Ankit Dave
comments.ai_summary: Ankit Dave is an EB-5 investor who filed in 2025 for $800K in a TEA. He asks USCIS to add a clear rule that if you filed before the new rule starts, your case is judged by the old rules from I-526E all the way to I-829.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person wrote in. They say 2 years is too short for the money to stay and create real jobs and point to Portugal which needs 5 years. They also say many comments asking for money back come from one Yellowstone project.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person filed a long legal comment. They say the rule defines fraud words clearly but does not define national security or public safety words, and they say the rule quietly removes protections that let investors see and answer negative information.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Harry Saltzgaver
comments.ai_summary: Harry Saltzgaver wrote about infrastructure projects. He asks USCIS to give clearer examples of what counts as an infrastructure project and to let private builders, not just government agencies, approve financing deals.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous .
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous conditional green card holder wrote in. They say they invested under old rules and worry new bridge loan rules will be applied late at I-829. They ask USCIS to limit but not ban bridge loans, with at least 36 months to match real building times.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor whose project was already approved wrote in. They ask USCIS to apply the new job rules about bridge loans and visitor spending only to future investors, not to people already in the program.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor who has not yet filed I-829 wrote in. They support program integrity but ask USCIS to make sure three new changes are not used to punish investors who already committed money and followed the old approved rules.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor filed a full analysis with proposed text. They ask USCIS to judge people who filed before the final rule under the old job methods, TEA data, and evidence lists, and to not deny an investor if the regional center misses a new form.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Amit Bhadauria
comments.ai_summary: Amit Bhadauria invested $800K into a rural Montana project in 2025. He supports the proposed 2-year sustainment starting when money is deployed and asks USCIS to keep that rule.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor wrote in. They ask USCIS to clearly say the new job rules about bridge loans and but-for tests will not be used at I-829 for projects that were already approved under old rules.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor wrote about source of funds paperwork. They say USCIS should not make them prove where every dollar in the company came from, including other investors not seeking visas, because that is not workable.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Lila Z
comments.ai_summary: Lila Z filed a comment with two main issues. She says the proposed 2-year rule creates two tracks that may treat rural and other investors unfairly, and she asks USCIS to make sustainment fair, clear, and not tied to visa backlogs.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by NIKHIL SP
comments.ai_summary: Nikhil SP wrote about bridge loans. He says banning repaid bridge loans hurts existing applicants and regional centers who planned jobs and financing around long-time USCIS policy that allowed them.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by University Beach Cooperative District
comments.ai_summary: University Beach Cooperative District is a local public group in Texas. They filed a comment about public works and infrastructure projects and how EB-5 can support them, with details in their attached PDF.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Kaushik K
comments.ai_summary: Kaushik K is an EB-5 investor. He says he supports integrity but strongly opposes removing bridge financing for job creation because it is needed to start projects early and was allowed before.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous existing investor wrote in worried about bridge loans. They say applying a new ban to people who already invested could hurt their immigration case and cause money loss.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by University Beach Cooperative District
comments.ai_summary: University Beach Cooperative District filed another comment. They again discuss public works projects as qualifying infrastructure, with more detail in the attached file.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Visa Franchise
comments.ai_summary: Visa Franchise helps foreign nationals buy U.S. franchises. They say direct EB-5 investors who run one small business are different from large regional center pools and ask USCIS to keep rules practical for them.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Wright Goforth
comments.ai_summary: Wright Goforth is a law firm. They filed a comment asking USCIS to define more clearly what counts as an infrastructure project under the new rule.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Robert Green
comments.ai_summary: Robert Green filed a formal comment. He says his full legal arguments are in the attached PDF on the government site.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous immigration lawyer with 15 years of EB-5 work wrote in. They ask about material change and capital rules and say many H-1B professionals who invested in good faith should not be penalized for normal business changes.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor wrote about the 2-year sustainment clock. They say USCIS should clearly state the clock starts when capital is deployed to the job-creating company, and the rule should cover post-RIA regional center investors.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person wrote about full-time jobs. They ask USCIS to keep allowing job sharing where two part-time workers count as one full-time job, because many small direct businesses rely on it.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Prashil Sureja
comments.ai_summary: Prashil Sureja invested $800K into Yellowstone Club Phase II in Big Sky in 2025. He strongly supports the 2-year sustainment measured from deployment and asks USCIS to finalize that approach.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by N O
comments.ai_summary: N O is a commenter who opposes parts of the rule. They say giving DHS wide power to fine, suspend, or debar regional centers without clear checks could be abused and hurt good-faith investors.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person says the change will hurt the U.S. economy. They worry it will keep many investors from putting money into U.S. markets and slow local growth.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor with a pending adjustment application thanked USCIS. They support stronger integrity and transparency and ask USCIS to protect good-faith investors as it updates the rules.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Jie Zhu
comments.ai_summary: Jie Zhu wrote about fund administrators. He asks USCIS to explain how a fund administrator actually signs on bank accounts and approves transfers, like whether it needs a bank signature card or an electronic sign-off.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person strongly supports ending repaid bridge financing. They say using EB-5 money just to repay an old loan is not what the program is for and can be abused.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person strongly supports a sustainment period longer than 2 years. They say the program should reward long-term investment that creates lasting jobs, not just a quick path to a green card.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person wrote about keeping your place in line. They support protecting investors when a regional center closes through no fault of the investor, but say the new rule should set a fair standard for who gets to keep their priority date.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Rajasekar Chinnasmay
comments.ai_summary: Rajasekar Chinnasmay invested $800K and his family already has conditional green cards. He says he relied on USCIS guidance that sustainment is about 2 years from deployment and asks USCIS to keep that promise.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor filed a follow-up on what counts as a qualifying investment. They ask USCIS to explain how the law applies when a good-faith investor needs to amend or move to a new investment if the first project fails.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Sameer Mehta
comments.ai_summary: Sameer Mehta is an investor. He asks USCIS to release his $800K after 2 years so he can use it to start a business and help the economy.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by LINNET JOSE
comments.ai_summary: Linnet Jose is an investor who put money in with a 2-year plan. She says 2 years makes sense for job creation and her family planned to use the returned money for kids' education.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Satya Vadapalli
comments.ai_summary: Satya Vadapalli is an investor. He asks USCIS to make a clear rule that sustainment ends 2 years after deployment. He says that treats people from all countries fairly even when visas are backed up.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Jenson Thottian
comments.ai_summary: Jenson Thottian invested $800K in Yellowstone Big Sky. He opposes making the sustainment period longer and says he chose this project because the rules clearly said 2 years.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor says he supports the 2-year sustainment rule starting when money reaches the job company. He invested expecting at least 2 years at risk, not an open-ended hold.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor put $800K plus about $50K in fees into Yellowstone Big Sky. He says his papers promised 2 years from deployment and asks USCIS not to change that after he relied on it.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous investor wrote about trusts and retirement accounts. They ask if money from a trust or IRA counts as capital and ask USCIS to explain how the September 30 2026 grandfathering date applies.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Rama Tejaswini  Thotapalli
comments.ai_summary: Rama Tejaswini Thotapalli invested $800K in Montana because 2 years gave her confidence her money would not be locked forever. She says she might not have invested if the rule was open-ended, and notes long waits for Indian investors.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous advocate wrote in strong support of the NPRM. They say the rule rightly cracks down on misuse by large operators and protects workers and program integrity.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Joydeep Das
comments.ai_summary: Joydeep Das is an investor. He says ending bridge financing will create big problems for people who already filed, because regional centers built their project budgets and job plans around earlier USCIS filings.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Falguni Gandhi
comments.ai_summary: Falguni Gandhi is an investor. She asks USCIS to release her investment in 2 years so she can build a better life in the U.S. and says she trusted the RIA rules when she invested.

comments.title: Comment Submitted by Anonymous
comments.ai_summary: An anonymous person wrote about protections for good-faith investors. They ask USCIS to clarify that someone who invested honestly can keep eligibility, amend, or move to a new investment if needed, and still remove conditions.
